subject: Pen test/inspection scope — limited inspection & order form redlines
messages:
From: Angela Meyer <angela@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Chu <michael.chu@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test and SOC2 evidence cadence — initial asks

Jonas,

Thanks for the draft order form. A couple of items our security team pulled out that we need to resolve before legal moves forward:

- Penetration test notice & scope: we need a limited-inspection option (sample-based, no live admin access) for our vendors. Can Redwood accept a confined inspection model instead of full inspection rights?
- SOC 2 evidence cadence: we typically ask for annual SOC 2 + a summary of remedial items for any significant control deficiencies. Can you confirm retention of the SOC 2 report and a timeline for providing it?
- Proof-of-pen-test: high-level pen-test summary (findings & remediation status) rather than full reports is acceptable, but we need to agree on a 30-day remediation reporting cadence for critical/high findings.

If you’re open to a redline where we add a limited-inspection carve-out and an explicit 30-day remediation update for critical issues, Legal should be able to proceed. Attaching our security checklist for reference.

Appreciate a quick turn here — targeting final MSA/order form this month.

Best,
Angela
Angela Meyer
Sr. InfoSec Manager | Cardinal Health
Attachment: Cardinal_Security_Checklist_20270512.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Angela Meyer <angela@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test and SOC2 evidence cadence — initial asks

On Wed, May 12, 2027 at 09:15 AM Angela Meyer <angela@cardinalhealth.com> wrote:
> Jonas,
>
> Thanks for the draft order form. A couple of items our security team pulled out that we need to resolve before legal moves forward:
>
> - Penetration test notice & scope: we need a limited-inspection option (sample-based, no live admin access) for our vendors. Can Redwood accept a confined inspection model instead of full inspection rights?
> - SOC 2 evidence cadence: we typically ask for annual SOC 2 + a summary of remedial items for any significant control deficiencies. Can you confirm retention of the SOC 2 report and a timeline for providing it?
> - Proof-of-pen-test: high-level pen-test summary (findings & remediation status) rather than full reports is acceptable, but we need to agree on a 30-day remediation reporting cadence for critical/high findings.

Thanks for the clear ask, Angela — this is helpful. Short answers up front:
- We can offer a limited inspection (sample-based) option for customers who require it; we would document the constraints (no admin shell access, observation only, scope bounded to production tenancy) in the security exhibit.
- Redwood retains the SOC 2 Type II report and can provide a copy under NDA; we can commit to delivering the latest report within 10 business days of request and to a quarterly status note for any repeated/ongoing remediation items.
- We can provide a high-level pen-test executive summary and remediation status for critical/high items. A 30-day cadence for status updates on critical findings is reasonable; for high/medium we usually run a 60–90 day window depending on complexity.

I'll loop in Legal to get their input on precise contract language and will send a proposed redline.

Next steps: I’m sending an internal request to Legal (cc'd) with our proposed exhibit language and a suggested limited-inspection clause. If that looks good to you, we’ll circulate a redline by EOD Friday.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0148
Attachment: redwood_security_exhibit_draft_v1.docx (docx)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Angela Meyer <angela@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pen test and SOC2 evidence cadence — proposed redlines (please review)

Laura / Olga — forwarding Cardinal's asks. High-level guidance from product: we can accept a limited-inspection mode and commit to the SOC 2 delivery timeline noted below. Please see the attached initial exhibit draft (redwood_security_exhibit_draft_v1.docx).

Key negotiation points I expect Legal to weigh in on:
- Wording for "limited inspection": define observation-only, sample size (e.g., up to 5 systems / 2 hours each), and no live admin activity.
- Redaction and confidentiality: we should retain discretion to redact sensitive infrastructure detail and withhold raw pen-test artifacts.
- Remediation cadence: agree on 30 days for critical, 60 days for high as a target, with exceptions allowed if agreed in writing.

Could you please: (1) scan the draft and propose contract-level redlines, (2) advise whether we can sign off on the 10-business-day SOC2 delivery commitment, and (3) confirm if the "limited inspection" carve-out is acceptable with the suggested guardrails.

Thanks — customer is pushing calendar for this month.
Jonas

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Angela Meyer <angela@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2027 11:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pen test and SOC2 evidence cadence — proposed redlines (please review)

Jonas / Olga / Angela — scanned the draft and added redlines. Summary of our positions:
1) Limited Inspection: Accept in principle. We will commit to an "inspection-lite" with the following contract language: observation-only, up to 5 named assets or application endpoints (customer to propose), sessions scheduled in mutually-agreed 2-hour blocks, and Redwood reserves the right to refuse disruptive activities.
2) Pen-test report handling: We will provide an executive summary of findings and remediation status. Full raw reports will be provided only under a mutually executed NDA and specifically limited to the customer’s tenancy.
3) Remediation cadence: We can commit to 30 days for Critical findings, 60 days for High findings, subject to documented exceptions (complex third-party fixes, etc.). We will also add language requiring notification to customer within 5 business days of a Critical finding.
4) SOC 2: We can deliver the SOC 2 Type II report within 10 business days of a written request under the existing confidentiality framework.

I've attached our redlined MSA exhibit and a separate short form that captures the inspection-lite parameters (MSA_Exhibit_Redlines_20270516.docx). Please review — if Cardinal agrees to the wording, Legal is prepared to finalize and route via DocuSign.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: MSA_Exhibit_Redlines_20270516.docx (docx)

From: Michael Chu <michael.chu@cardinalhealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Angela Meyer <angela@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test and SOC2 evidence cadence — Cardinal counterpoints

Thanks, Laura. We appreciate Redwood moving on limited inspection and the SOC2 timeline. A few counterpoints from our side:

- Sample size: we trust Redwood's right to refuse disruptive tests, but we ask the contract to include a minimum sample of 3 specified assets or endpoints (customer-specified) to ensure the inspection is meaningful.
- Notice period for pen-test window: our security team prefers a 10-business-day notice. Redwood's 2-hour block model works operationally, but we want enough lead time to prepare an internal schedule and raise any concerns.
- Remediation evidence: 30 days for critical is acceptable only if Redwood provides a written remediation plan within 7 calendar days. That plan should include owner, mitigation steps, and an expected completion date.

Attached are our annotated redlines (Cardinal_Redlines_20270518.pdf). If Redwood is good with the 3-asset minimum and 10-business-day notice, we can sign the exhibit and move forward with the order form.

-Michael
Michael Chu
Sr. Procurement Manager | Cardinal Health
Attachment: Cardinal_Redlines_20270518.pdf (pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Angela Meyer <angela@cardinalhealth.com>, Michael Chu <michael.chu@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final confine-inspection alignment & next steps

Michael / Angela — thanks for the quick turn and the annotated redlines. Short response and next steps below:

- Sample minimum: Redwood can accept a customer-specified minimum of 3 assets/endpoints for the limited inspection. We'll include that in the exhibit language.
- Notice period: 10 business days' advance notice is fine for scheduling. We will keep the 2-hour mutually-agreeable sessions inside that window.
- Remediation evidence: We agree to provide a written remediation plan within 7 calendar days for Critical findings and a status update cadence of 30 days thereafter. We'll add a short template for the remediation plan into the exhibit to make expectations explicit.

Next steps: Laura will finalize the redlines in the attached MSA exhibit and route via DocuSign. Expect the DocuSign packet by tomorrow (link: https://app.docusign.com/sign/xyz-123). Please confirm you’re comfortable with the redlines once you receive the packet and we’ll execute.

Thanks — moving this across the finish line.
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: msas_orderform_v3_redlines.docx (docx)
